heading: South Carolina Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **South Carolina paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, South Carolina income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

South Carolina introduced significant income tax reforms in 2026. Understanding the difference between its annual income tax rules and employer payroll withholding methods is important when estimating your net earnings.

Whether you work in Charleston, Columbia, Greenville, Spartanburg or another South Carolina community, this calculator can help you compare salary offers and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the South Carolina Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your earnings before taxes and deductions. Hourly employees should include regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Choose your payment frequency. Enter federal and South Carolina income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Add retirement contributions and health insurance premiums. Enter the full tax amounts, including any extra withholding.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown to understand individual deductions and remaining take-home income.

For greater accuracy, enter information from your latest payroll statement and withholding certificates.

## South Carolina Payroll Taxes in 2026

Your actual deductions depend on taxable earnings, withholding allowances, payment frequency and employee benefits.

Visit the [South Carolina Department of Revenue withholding page](https://dor.sc.gov/withholding) for current employer withholding tables, formulas and employee certificates.

## South Carolina's 2026 Income Tax Changes

South Carolina enacted significant individual income tax reforms through H.4216, signed into law on March 30, 2026.

The legislation introduced two annual individual income tax brackets.

These rules apply to the 2026 income tax year.

However, they should not automatically be used as a replacement for the official 2026 employer payroll withholding formula.

Payroll withholding and annual income tax liability are different calculations.

Read the official [South Carolina H.4216 announcement](https://dor.sc.gov/news/information-about-h-4216) and [South Carolina individual income tax guidance](https://dor.sc.gov/IIT) for details.

## Understanding the South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction

The new legislation introduced the South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction, commonly abbreviated SCIAD.

It replaces the state's previous reliance on federal standard and itemized deductions for annual income tax purposes.

The initial deduction amounts are:

These amounts may be reduced based on applicable income thresholds.

The deduction affects the calculation of annual South Carolina taxable income. It is not a separate cash deduction from your paycheck.

Consult the [South Carolina Department of Revenue legislative update](https://dor.sc.gov/administrative-legislative-regulations-tax-legislation-update-2026) for additional information about the reform.

## How South Carolina Paycheck Withholding Works

South Carolina publishes a separate employer withholding formula.

Under the published 2026 formula, each applicable personal withholding allowance has an annual value of $5,000.

Employees claiming at least one allowance also receive a withholding deduction equal to 10% of annualized wages, limited to $7,500.

Employees claiming zero allowances do not receive these allowance-based deductions under the published formula.

Employers subtract the applicable amounts from annualized wages before applying the relevant withholding calculation.

Review the official [2026 South Carolina withholding formula, WH-1603F](https://dor.sc.gov/sites/dor/files/forms/WH1603F_2026.pdf) for the complete methodology.

## South Carolina Withholding Allowance Example

Suppose an employee earns $65,000 annually and claims one qualifying withholding allowance.

Annualized taxable wages: $65,000.

Personal withholding allowance: $5,000.

Applicable withholding deduction:

$65,000 × 10% = $6,500.

Adjusted annual wages:

$65,000 − $5,000 − $6,500 = $53,500.

The employer then applies the relevant 2026 withholding rate schedule and converts the result into the appropriate payroll period.

This example demonstrates how withholding allowances affect the wage amount used to calculate payroll taxes.

The $53,500 figure is adjusted income for the employer withholding calculation. It is not necessarily the employee's final annual taxable income under the new tax legislation.

## Understanding South Carolina Form SC W-4

South Carolina employees generally complete Form SC W-4 to communicate their state withholding information to employers.

The form records applicable withholding allowances and additional withholding requests.

Federal Form W-4 is separate from the South Carolina certificate.

Employees with multiple jobs, working spouses or significant changes in household circumstances should review their withholding elections carefully.

Reducing paycheck withholding increases immediate take-home pay but may not reduce final annual income tax liability.

Access the current SC W-4 through the official [South Carolina withholding resources](https://dor.sc.gov/withholding).

## Federal Taxes Deducted From South Carolina Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

Multiple jobs, eligible credits, other income and additional withholding requests can affect the amount deducted.

Employers follow the official calculation procedures in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

The [IRS Tax Withholding Estimator](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-withholding-estimator) can help employees evaluate their federal withholding arrangements.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered earnings toward Social Security.

For 2026, the annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500.

An employee receiving $2,500 in covered wages before reaching the annual ceiling would contribute $155.

Visit the [Social Security Administration contribution and benefit base page](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html) for annual wage limit information.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages without a standard annual taxable wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when covered Medicare wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for additional federal payroll information.

## South Carolina Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually before taxes and deductions.
Assume ordinary single federal withholding settings, a modern Form W-4 without additional adjustments and no benefit deductions.

Approximately $2,092.60 remains before South Carolina income tax and other employee deductions.

To determine your complete estimated take-home pay, enter the state withholding amount shown on your pay stub.

Your actual paycheck depends on withholding allowances, benefits and other employment circumstances.

## South Carolina Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can calculate gross earnings using regular working hours and qualifying overtime compensation.

Suppose an employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus eight qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000.

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 8 = $300.

Total gross earnings: $1,300.

Assuming all earnings are covered by ordinary federal payroll contributions:

Social Security: $80.60.

Medicare: $18.85.

Approximately $1,200.55 remains before federal income tax, South Carolina income tax and other deductions.

Consult the [South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation](https://llr.sc.gov/) and [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable employment requirements.

## Does South Carolina Have Local Income Taxes?

South Carolina municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employee compensation.

Employees working in Charleston, Columbia or Greenville therefore generally do not encounter municipal wage income taxes of the kind found in some Pennsylvania or Ohio communities.

However, housing costs, transportation expenses, insurance premiums and local sales taxes can affect disposable income.

When comparing employment opportunities, calculate your estimated net salary first and then evaluate location-specific expenses.

## Working Across South Carolina State Borders

South Carolina employees may live in North Carolina or Georgia while working in South Carolina, or work outside South Carolina while residing within the state.

These arrangements may create different withholding and annual tax filing requirements.

Applicable resident tax credits may help reduce double taxation.

However, interstate employees should not assume that living in another state automatically eliminates South Carolina income tax on qualifying South Carolina-sourced wages.

Visit the [South Carolina Department of Revenue](https://dor.sc.gov/) for residency and income sourcing guidance.

## Managing Your South Carolina Take-Home Pay

Build your monthly budget using estimated net earnings rather than your gross annual salary.

Account for housing, groceries, transportation, utilities, healthcare and required debt payments.

Compare retirement matching, insurance costs and paid leave benefits when evaluating employment opportunities.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a savings target, while our [debt-to-income ratio calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate borrowing commitments.

The [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/) also provides resources for managing household finances.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is South Carolina's income tax rate in 2026?

The new annual income tax structure uses a 1.99% rate below $30,000 in taxable income and a 5.21% calculation minus $966 at or above $30,000. Paycheck withholding follows the separate official employer formula.

### How much is a South Carolina withholding allowance worth?

Under the published 2026 employer formula, each qualifying personal withholding allowance reduces annualized wages by $5,000.

### Does South Carolina have local employee income taxes?

South Carolina municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes. Applicable federal and state taxes still reduce employee earnings.
